item.stdout:
Manage GitHub-mirror placements on EntireDB clusters

Usage:
  entire repo mirror [command]

Available Commands:
  collaborators List the users with access to a mirror (live GitHub-admin gated)
  create        Register a GitHub mirror on a cluster
  get           Show a repo's mirrors by owner/repo, or one mirror by ULID or clone URL
  list          List repos you can see: existing mirrors and GitHub repos you could onboard
  remove        Un-register a GitHub mirror from a cluster
  use           Point this clone's git remote at an Entire mirror

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for mirror

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Use "entire repo mirror [command] --help" for more information about a command.
List repos visible from your login in one table: existing mirrors (one row per repo, with the clusters it is mirrored on and the clone status) and GitHub repos you could onboard (access, availability). Sparse cells show '-'. Per-cluster detail and clone URLs: `entire repo mirror get <owner/repo>`.

The first 1000 entries are fetched by default, with a note on stderr when more exist. Filters and --sort apply to those fetched rows — add --all to work over the complete list, or --limit N for just the first N.

For manual paging, --page-size/--page-token fetch one page at a time; with --json the rows come wrapped in an {items, nextPageToken} envelope.

Usage:
  entire repo mirror list [flags]

Navigation Flags:
      --all                 Fetch the complete directory instead of the first 1000 entries (slower on large orgs)
      --limit int           Show at most N rows, applied after the local filters and sort (0 shows all fetched)
      --page-size int       Fetch a single page of at most N entries (1-500; the server may cap N further) and print the resume cursor
      --page-token string   Fetch the single page at this cursor (from a previous run's nextPageToken)

Filtering & Sorting Flags:
  Applied only to the fetched rows; combine with --all to filter/sort the complete mirror list.
      --access string    Filter by exact ACCESS (candidates only: read/write/admin)
      --available        Keep only GitHub repos you could onboard as mirrors (drops existing mirrors)
      --cluster string   Keep only repos mirrored on this cluster, by slug or public host (drops onboardable candidates)
      --mirrored         Keep only repos already mirrored (drops onboardable candidates)
      --name string      Filter by owner/repo substring, matching the NAME column (case-insensitive)
      --owner string     Filter by upstream owner login
      --private          Filter by visibility: --private for private only, --private=false for public only (omit for all)
      --sort string      Sort by column key (e.g. name, clusters; prefix '-' for descending). Default: name ascending
      --status string    Filter by exact STATUS (mirrors: ready/processing/failed/suspended, matching any of a repo's placements; candidates: available/owner-only)

Formatting Flags:
      --json       Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --no-pager   Print directly to stdout instead of a pager for long output

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for list

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

Usage:
  entire api <path> [flags]

Examples:
  entire api /api/v1/clusters
  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --to cell "/api/v1/me/recap?repo={repo_id}"
  entire api -X POST /api/v1/projects -f name=demo

Flags:
  -F, --field stringArray       add a typed parameter in key=value format; true/false/null/numbers are converted (repeatable)
  -H, --header stringArray      add a request header in key:value format (repeatable)
  -h, --help                    help for api
  -i, --include                 print the response status line and headers too
      --input string            file with the request body ("-" for stdin)
  -j, --jurisdiction string     target a specific jurisdiction's cell (e.g. us, eu) instead of your home cell; implies --to cell
  -X, --method string           HTTP method (default GET, or POST when a field/body is given)
  -f, --raw-field stringArray   add a string parameter in key=value format (repeatable)
      --to string               which backend to call: core or cell (default "core")

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Show a mirror, or every mirror of a repo. <mirror> is one of:

  - <owner>/<repo>, as shown in the `mirror list` NAME column — shows the
    repo (visibility, access) and its mirror on every cluster, with
    per-cluster clone URL and status
  - a mirror ULID
  - an entire:// clone URL (entire://<cluster>/gh/<owner>/<repo>) — the form
    `git clone` accepts; a trailing .git, as pasted from `git remote -v`, is
    accepted too

A clone URL is looked up on the login server fronting its cluster, so it
resolves even when that cluster belongs to a federation other than the active
auth context; an owner/repo or ULID is looked up on the active context's
login server.

Usage:
  entire repo mirror get <mirror> [flags]

Examples:
  entire repo mirror get octocat/hello-world
  entire repo mirror get 01KS6KFJR2XS6PZ188MVYE07AN
  entire repo mirror get entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/gh/octocat/hello-world

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for get
      --json   Output raw JSON instead of a table

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

# SHIFT Buildathon Evidence

SHIFT is a requirement-change control layer for AI coding agents. It turns a
new requirement, checkpoint-backed historical intent, and Entire Graph
structural evidence into a pre-change contract, then deterministically verifies
the implementation against that same contract.

## Milestone 1: Initial understanding and architecture

Recorded before product implementation in the fresh post-Graph-activation
Codex session.

### Required environment checks

- Mirror clone: `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`
- Entire status: enabled on `main`; Codex is enabled; checkpoint sync target is
  `origin`.
- Entire Graph version: `v0.4.0`.
- Graph capabilities report Go semantic relations including definitions,
  calls, type use, field access, data flow, test relationships, and semantic
  diff support.

The `entire` executable was not present on this PowerShell process's `PATH`, so
development evidence uses the installed absolute binary at
`C:\Users\DELL\.local\bin\entire.exe`. This is an environment constraint, not
evidence that Graph is unavailable.

### Architecture decision

The implementation will stay native to the existing Go/Cobra CLI and separate
the responsibilities that the PRD identifies:

1. a `shift` Cobra group with non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands;
2. a structured contract model and deterministic status reducer;
3. checkpoint retrieval through Entire's existing checkpoint readers rather
   than direct parsing of checkpoint Git storage;
4. a Graph adapter that invokes the installed `entire graph` surface and keeps
   failures explicitly `UNVERIFIED`;
5. deterministic Markdown/JSON artifact rendering under `.shift/`;
6. verification driven by explicit evidence inputs and test-command results;
7. a small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified paths.

Checkpoint provenance is load-bearing: an invariant cannot be marked
`EXPLICIT` without a successfully read checkpoint and a source reference.
Graph output remains structural evidence and never substitutes for source or
test proof.

### Early Entire Graph evidence

Command:

```text
entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query \
  "native Cobra command registration and checkpoint reading for shift analyze verify"
```

The search indexed the mirror at commit `3dbdf8b83c39ef7ae73b9c613612f4c51aff3f1a`
and returned these relevant existing seams:

- `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`, the shared reader
  abstraction that normalizes missing checkpoints and wraps reader errors;
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:693` — the existing local checkpoint lookup and
  explanation path;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit.go:54` — construction of checkpoint
  stores with the elected read-remotes chain;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:314` — checkpoint listing metadata.

The top-ranked result was an API response identity validator, so rank alone was
not treated as an architecture decision. The focused source and neighboring
callers must determine the reusable local reader path.

## Remaining required evidence

- Graph relationship/impact analysis before the checkpoint/command integration
  change.
- Graph semantic diff after implementation.
- Stable implementation, curveball-response, and final-verification Entire
  checkpoint milestones.

content.text:
1. What SHIFT is intended to do

SHIFT is a native Entire CLI requirement-change control layer. It combines:

- A new requirement
- Checkpoint-backed historical intent and invariants
- Entire Graph structural evidence
- Source and test evidence

It produces a pre-implementation Change Contract, then verifies the resulting change as `CHANGE VERIFIED`, `CHANGE BLOCKED`, or `VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE`.

2. Architecture chosen so far

- Native Go/Cobra `entire shift` command group.
- Non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands.
- Structured contract and verification models.
- Existing Entire checkpoint readers for historical evidence.
- A Graph adapter with explicit `UNVERIFIED` degradation.
- Deterministic Markdown/JSON output under `.shift/`.
- Evidence-driven verification and test-result handling.
- A small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified transitions.

3. What has actually been implemented

- Fork confirmed: `aviraj-singh1/cli`.
- India mirror created on `aws-ap-south-1`.
- Repository cloned through Entire into `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`.
- Entire enabled for Codex.
- Entire Graph `v0.4.0` activated and agent instructions generated.
- A fresh post-activation agent session was started.
- Graph search and `ReadCheckpoint` definition investigation were performed.
- Initial architecture and Graph evidence were documented and committed.
- Commit: `d401dedcc` — `docs(shift): capture initial architecture checkpoint`
- No SHIFT product code or tests have been implemented.

4. Files changed

Committed:

- `BUILDATHON.md`

Uncommitted setup changes created by Entire/Graph activation:

- `.codex/hooks.json`
- `.entire/settings.json`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `.entire/graph-agent.md` — currently untracked

5. Existing Entire CLI components/packages planned for reuse

- `api/checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint`
- Existing checkpoint `PersistentStore` and session-reader interfaces
- `checkpoint.Open`
- `strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes`
- Local checkpoint lookup patterns in `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go`
- Checkpoint-store construction in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit.go`
- Checkpoint metadata listing in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go`
- Existing Cobra command registration conventions
- Installed `entire graph` command surface

6. What is incomplete

- `entire shift analyze`
- `entire shift verify`
- Contract and verification data models
- Checkpoint evidence extraction
- Graph adapter
- Markdown/JSON rendering
- Deterministic verification reducer
- Authentication demo fixture
- Unit, provenance, uncertainty, Graph-integration, and end-to-end tests
- Pre-edit Graph impact analysis for the Privacy Boundary
- Privacy/redaction adaptation
- Final Graph semantic diff
- Curveball-response and final checkpoints

7. Current assumptions and technical risks

- An invariant may be `EXPLICIT` only when supported by successfully read checkpoint evidence and provenance.
- Graph output is evidence, not authoritative proof.
- Missing Graph, checkpoint, transcript, source, or test evidence must produce `UNVERIFIED` or incomplete output.
- Explicit checkpoint input remains the safest P0 path.
- Commands should remain non-interactive and agent-consumable.
- The privacy curveball invalidates any assumption that complete raw prompts/transcripts are always available or may be sent to another service.
- The current implementation does not yet handle redacted or missing checkpoint fields.
- Entire reports seven Codex hooks still needing approval.
- `entire status` confirms Entire is enabled but did not visibly confirm a checkpoint ID for commit `d401dedcc`; checkpoint creation must be verified before reconstruction.
- The branch is one commit ahead of `origin/main`, with the setup files still uncommitted.

types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

---GRAPH-AGENT---
# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in settings. Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository.

This is useful when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves
and makes changes in another. Adoption moves the live session state into the
current repo and seeds it with the current repo's uncommitted file changes so
the next commit can be linked normally.

When the source and target share a Git session store, adoption moves the same
session state file to the current worktree and requires --force or --yes.

Usage:
  entire session adopt [session-id] [flags]

Examples:
  entire session adopt 019ed5fe-ec49-7a72-89fd-f38e323f5448 --from ../cli
  entire session adopt --from /path/to/source/worktree
  entire session adopt --from ../source-worktree --yes

Flags:
      --force         replace an existing local state file for the same session
      --from string   source worktree that already tracks the session
  -h, --help          help for adopt
      --yes           confirm same-store adoption and replacement without prompting

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in settings. Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
Adopt an active session from another worktree into the current repository.

This is useful when an agent starts in one repository or worktree, then moves
and makes changes in another. Adoption moves the live session state into the
current repo and seeds it with the current repo's uncommitted file changes so
the next commit can be linked normally.

When the source and target share a Git session store, adoption moves the same
session state file to the current worktree and requires --force or --yes.

Usage:
  entire session adopt [session-id] [flags]

Examples:
  entire session adopt 019ed5fe-ec49-7a72-89fd-f38e323f5448 --from ../cli
  entire session adopt --from /path/to/source/worktree
  entire session adopt --from ../source-worktree --yes

Flags:
      --force         replace an existing local state file for the same session
      --from string   source worktree that already tracks the session
  -h, --help          help for adopt

Global Flags:

---COMMITTED BUILDATHON STATE---
# SHIFT Buildathon Evidence

SHIFT is a requirement-change control layer for AI coding agents. It turns a
new requirement, checkpoint-backed historical intent, and Entire Graph
structural evidence into a pre-change contract, then deterministically verifies
the implementation against that same contract.

## Milestone 1: Initial understanding and architecture

Recorded before product implementation in the fresh post-Graph-activation
Codex session.

### Required environment checks

- Mirror clone: `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`
- Entire status: enabled on `main`; Codex is enabled; checkpoint sync target is
  `origin`.
- Entire Graph version: `v0.4.0`.
- Graph capabilities report Go semantic relations including definitions,
  calls, type use, field access, data flow, test relationships, and semantic
  diff support.

The `entire` executable was not present on this PowerShell process's `PATH`, so
development evidence uses the installed absolute binary at
`C:\Users\DELL\.local\bin\entire.exe`. This is an environment constraint, not
evidence that Graph is unavailable.

### Architecture decision

The implementation will stay native to the existing Go/Cobra CLI and separate
the responsibilities that the PRD identifies:

1. a `shift` Cobra group with non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands;
2. a structured contract model and deterministic status reducer;
3. checkpoint retrieval through Entire's existing checkpoint readers rather
   than direct parsing of checkpoint Git storage;
4. a Graph adapter that invokes the installed `entire graph` surface and keeps
   failures explicitly `UNVERIFIED`;
5. deterministic Markdown/JSON artifact rendering under `.shift/`;
6. verification driven by explicit evidence inputs and test-command results;
7. a small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified paths.

Checkpoint provenance is load-bearing: an invariant cannot be marked
`EXPLICIT` without a successfully read checkpoint and a source reference.
Graph output remains structural evidence and never substitutes for source or
test proof.

### Early Entire Graph evidence

Command:

```text
entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query \
  "native Cobra command registration and checkpoint reading for shift analyze verify"
```

The search indexed the mirror at commit `3dbdf8b83c39ef7ae73b9c613612f4c51aff3f1a`
and returned these relevant existing seams:

- `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`, the shared reader
  abstraction that normalizes missing checkpoints and wraps reader errors;
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:693` — the existing local checkpoint lookup and
  explanation path;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit.go:54` — construction of checkpoint
  stores with the elected read-remotes chain;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:314` — checkpoint listing metadata.

The top-ranked result was an API response identity validator, so rank alone was
not treated as an architecture decision. The focused source and neighboring
callers must determine the reusable local reader path.

## Remaining required evidence

- Graph relationship/impact analysis before the checkpoint/command integration
  change.
- Graph semantic diff after implementation.
- Stable implementation, curveball-response, and final-verification Entire
  checkpoint milestones.

---COMMITTED BUILDATHON STATE---
# SHIFT Buildathon Evidence

SHIFT is a requirement-change control layer for AI coding agents. It turns a
new requirement, checkpoint-backed historical intent, and Entire Graph
structural evidence into a pre-change contract, then deterministically verifies
the implementation against that same contract.

## Milestone 1: Initial understanding and architecture

Recorded before product implementation in the fresh post-Graph-activation
Codex session.

### Required environment checks

- Mirror clone: `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`
- Entire status: enabled on `main`; Codex is enabled; checkpoint sync target is
  `origin`.
- Entire Graph version: `v0.4.0`.
- Graph capabilities report Go semantic relations including definitions,
  calls, type use, field access, data flow, test relationships, and semantic
  diff support.

The `entire` executable was not present on this PowerShell process's `PATH`, so
development evidence uses the installed absolute binary at
`C:\Users\DELL\.local\bin\entire.exe`. This is an environment constraint, not
evidence that Graph is unavailable.

### Architecture decision

The implementation will stay native to the existing Go/Cobra CLI and separate
the responsibilities that the PRD identifies:

1. a `shift` Cobra group with non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands;
2. a structured contract model and deterministic status reducer;
3. checkpoint retrieval through Entire's existing checkpoint readers rather
   than direct parsing of checkpoint Git storage;
4. a Graph adapter that invokes the installed `entire graph` surface and keeps
   failures explicitly `UNVERIFIED`;
5. deterministic Markdown/JSON artifact rendering under `.shift/`;
6. verification driven by explicit evidence inputs and test-command results;
7. a small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified paths.

Checkpoint provenance is load-bearing: an invariant cannot be marked
`EXPLICIT` without a successfully read checkpoint and a source reference.
Graph output remains structural evidence and never substitutes for source or
test proof.

### Early Entire Graph evidence

Command:

```text
entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query \
  "native Cobra command registration and checkpoint reading for shift analyze verify"
```

The search indexed the mirror at commit `3dbdf8b83c39ef7ae73b9c613612f4c51aff3f1a`
and returned these relevant existing seams:

- `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`, the shared reader
  abstraction that normalizes missing checkpoints and wraps reader errors;
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:693` — the existing local checkpoint lookup and
  explanation path;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit.go:54` — construction of checkpoint
  stores with the elected read-remotes chain;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:314` — checkpoint listing metadata.

The top-ranked result was an API response identity validator, so rank alone was
not treated as an architecture decision. The focused source and neighboring
callers must determine the reusable local reader path.

## Remaining required evidence

- Graph relationship/impact analysis before the checkpoint/command integration
  change.
- Graph semantic diff after implementation.
- Stable implementation, curveball-response, and final-verification Entire
  checkpoint milestones.

---COMMITTED BUILDATHON STATE---
# SHIFT Buildathon Evidence

SHIFT is a requirement-change control layer for AI coding agents. It turns a
new requirement, checkpoint-backed historical intent, and Entire Graph
structural evidence into a pre-change contract, then deterministically verifies
the implementation against that same contract.

## Milestone 1: Initial understanding and architecture

Recorded before product implementation in the fresh post-Graph-activation
Codex session.

### Required environment checks

- Mirror clone: `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`
- Entire status: enabled on `main`; Codex is enabled; checkpoint sync target is
  `origin`.
- Entire Graph version: `v0.4.0`.
- Graph capabilities report Go semantic relations including definitions,
  calls, type use, field access, data flow, test relationships, and semantic
  diff support.

The `entire` executable was not present on this PowerShell process's `PATH`, so
development evidence uses the installed absolute binary at
`C:\Users\DELL\.local\bin\entire.exe`. This is an environment constraint, not
evidence that Graph is unavailable.

### Architecture decision

The implementation will stay native to the existing Go/Cobra CLI and separate
the responsibilities that the PRD identifies:

1. a `shift` Cobra group with non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands;
2. a structured contract model and deterministic status reducer;
3. checkpoint retrieval through Entire's existing checkpoint readers rather
   than direct parsing of checkpoint Git storage;
4. a Graph adapter that invokes the installed `entire graph` surface and keeps
   failures explicitly `UNVERIFIED`;
5. deterministic Markdown/JSON artifact rendering under `.shift/`;
6. verification driven by explicit evidence inputs and test-command results;
7. a small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified paths.

Checkpoint provenance is load-bearing: an invariant cannot be marked
`EXPLICIT` without a successfully read checkpoint and a source reference.
Graph output remains structural evidence and never substitutes for source or
test proof.

### Early Entire Graph evidence

Command:

```text
entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query \
  "native Cobra command registration and checkpoint reading for shift analyze verify"
```

The search indexed the mirror at commit `3dbdf8b83c39ef7ae73b9c613612f4c51aff3f1a`
and returned these relevant existing seams:

- `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`, the shared reader
  abstraction that normalizes missing checkpoints and wraps reader errors;
- `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:693` — the existing local checkpoint lookup and
  explanation path;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit.go:54` — construction of checkpoint
  stores with the elected read-remotes chain;
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:314` — checkpoint listing metadata.

The top-ranked result was an API response identity validator, so rank alone was
not treated as an architecture decision. The focused source and neighboring
callers must determine the reusable local reader path.

## Remaining required evidence

- Graph relationship/impact analysis before the checkpoint/command integration
  change.
- Graph semantic diff after implementation.
- Stable implementation, curveball-response, and final-verification Entire
  checkpoint milestones.

# SHIFT Buildathon Evidence

SHIFT is a requirement-change control layer for AI coding agents. It turns a
new requirement, checkpoint-backed historical intent, and Entire Graph
structural evidence into a pre-change contract, then deterministically verifies
the implementation against that same contract.

## Milestone 1: Initial understanding and architecture

Recorded before product implementation in the fresh post-Graph-activation
Codex session.

### Required environment checks

- Mirror clone: `C:\Users\DELL\Documents\SHIFT\cli`
- Entire status: enabled on `main`; Codex is enabled; checkpoint sync target is
  `origin`.
- Entire Graph version: `v0.4.0`.
- Graph capabilities report Go semantic relations including definitions,
  calls, type use, field access, data flow, test relationships, and semantic
  diff support.

The `entire` executable was not present on this PowerShell process's `PATH`, so
development evidence uses the installed absolute binary at
`C:\Users\DELL\.local\bin\entire.exe`. This is an environment constraint, not
evidence that Graph is unavailable.

### Architecture decision

The implementation will stay native to the existing Go/Cobra CLI and separate
the responsibilities that the PRD identifies:

1. a `shift` Cobra group with non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands;
2. a structured contract model and deterministic status reducer;
3. checkpoint retrieval through Entire's existing checkpoint readers rather
   than direct parsing of checkpoint Git storage;
4. a Graph adapter that invokes the installed `entire graph` surface and keeps
   failures explicitly `UNVERIFIED`;
5. deterministic Markdown/JSON artifact rendering under `.shift/`;
6. verification driven by explicit evidence inputs and test-command results;
7. a small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified paths.

Checkpoint provenance is load-bearing: an invariant cannot be marked
`EXPLICIT` without a successfully read checkpoint and a source reference.
Graph output remains structural evidence and never substitutes for source or
test proof.

No files were modified. Findings below come only from checkpoint `01M1TQJ0G9VWM44XTQTATJGV5Q`, commit `5e948e6d`, and read-only repository/Graph analysis.

## Pre-curveball reconstruction

1. SHIFT’s intended purpose

SHIFT is a native Entire CLI workflow for managing requirement changes in AI-assisted development.

It would:

- Read historical intent from Entire Checkpoints.
- Identify invariants and assumptions behind existing behavior.
- Compare them with a new requirement.
- Use Entire Graph for structural impact evidence.
- Generate a Change Contract before implementation.
- Verify the resulting implementation against the requirement, invariants, Graph evidence, source inspection, and tests.

Its three final outcomes were designed as:

- `CHANGE VERIFIED`
- `CHANGE BLOCKED`
- `VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE`

2. Selected architecture

The pre-curveball architecture separated these responsibilities:

- Native Go/Cobra `entire shift` command group.
- Non-interactive `analyze` and `verify` commands.
- Structured contract and verification models.
- Checkpoint retrieval through existing Entire checkpoint readers.
- Graph subprocess adapter with failures represented as `UNVERIFIED`.
- Deterministic Markdown and JSON artifacts under `.shift/`.
- Deterministic verification status reducer.
- Explicit evidence and test-result inputs.
- Small authentication fixture demonstrating blocked and verified changes.

Planned Entire CLI reuse included:

- `api/checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint`
- The existing checkpoint `PersistentStore`
- Session-content reader interfaces
- `checkpoint.Open`
- `strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes`
- Checkpoint lookup patterns in `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go`
- Existing Cobra command-registration conventions

3. What had actually been implemented

Only the initial architecture/evidence milestone was implemented.

Completed work:

- Entire enabled in the India-mirrored clone.
- Entire Graph `v0.4.0` activated.
- Initial Graph search and `ReadCheckpoint` definition lookup completed.
- Architecture and early Graph evidence recorded in `BUILDATHON.md`.
- That document was committed and linked to the checkpoint.

No SHIFT product command, model, renderer, verification logic, or test had been implemented.

4. What remained incomplete

- `entire shift analyze`
- `entire shift verify`
- Contract data model
- Verification data model and reducer
- Checkpoint evidence extraction
- Historical intent and invariant classification
- Invalidated-assumption analysis
- Graph adapter
- Markdown and JSON rendering
- `why` provenance output
- Authentication demo fixture
- Redacted or missing checkpoint fixture
- Unit, provenance, uncertainty, Graph-integration, and end-to-end tests
- Runtime/build verification
- Final semantic Graph diff
- Curveball-response and final checkpoints

5. Historical assumptions in the design

The architecture assumed:

- An invariant could be authoritative when a checkpoint was successfully read and a provenance reference existed.
- Checkpoint availability was primarily binary: found or missing.
- A successfully retrieved checkpoint would contain enough historical material for contract generation.
- Loaded transcript and prompt content could be treated as ordinary reasoning input.
- No separate field-level completeness or redaction model was necessary.
- Graph failures could be represented as `UNVERIFIED`.
- Explicit checkpoint input was sufficient for the P0 workflow.
- Commands should remain non-interactive and agent-consumable.
- Graph evidence must be verified against source and tests.

6. Known technical risks

- The original checkpoint had no generated summary; its structured intent was not useful, so reconstruction depended on transcript content.
- `ReadCheckpoint` distinguishes found from missing but does not establish that the returned historical context is complete.
- `SessionContent` exposes `Metadata`, `Transcript`, `TranscriptBlobHashes`, and `Prompts` without an explicit completeness classification.
- Entire’s configured summary path can pass a scoped transcript to a selected generator through `generateCheckpointSummary`.
- Graph ranking was known to be imperfect and required focused source verification.
- Graph reported one unrelated minified JSON parse failure, although its Go impact queries were complete.
- `mise`, `go`, and `gofmt` were unavailable in the checkpoint session, so no build or test had run.
- Seven Codex hooks were still awaiting approval.
- Windows-specific Entire/Graph setup changes remain uncommitted.

## Curveball analysis

### Exact invalidated assumption

The Curveball invalidates this original architectural assumption:

> A successfully retrieved checkpoint with provenance is sufficiently complete and safe to use as authoritative historical context.

That assumption combined two ideas which are no longer valid:

1. Retrieval success implied usable completeness.
2. Raw checkpoint prompts or transcripts could flow into the selected reasoning or summarization provider without a separate privacy boundary.

Under the new requirement, a checkpoint may exist while important fields are redacted or unavailable. A checkpoint ID and provenance reference therefore cannot, by themselves, justify an `EXPLICIT`, complete, or authoritative result.

### Required design change

SHIFT must introduce a first-class context-completeness boundary before historical evidence reaches contract reasoning.

At minimum, evidence needs distinctions such as:

- `COMPLETE`
- `PARTIAL_REDACTED`
- `PARTIAL_MISSING`
- `UNAVAILABLE`

Consequences:

- Redacted or missing evidence may still produce useful, clearly qualified findings.
- Claims derived from partial context cannot become authoritative historical invariants.
- Partial context must force relevant assertions to `INFERRED` or `UNVERIFIED`.
- Verification cannot return `CHANGE VERIFIED` when required historical evidence is incomplete.
- Raw prompts and transcripts must remain local unless an already-approved local processing path satisfies the privacy boundary.
- Any external reasoning path must receive only an explicitly safe, minimized representation—not raw transcript content.

### Graph-identified affected paths

Read-only Graph impact analysis identified these relevant existing paths:

- Checkpoint retrieval:
  - `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/aliases.go:66`

- Checkpoint content model:
  - `api/checkpoint/metadata.go:371` — `SessionContent`

- Existing summary/provider path:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1034` — `generateCheckpointSummary`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1111` — `maybeCompactExternalTranscript`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1196` — `generateCheckpointAISummary`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go:83` — provider resolution

- Existing redaction paths:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:442` — redaction configuration
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/redact_cache.go:500` — `RedactTranscriptCached`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/prompts.go:31` — `RedactedJoinedPrompts`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:2507` — redacted checkpoint blob creation
  - `redact/redact.go:112` — `AlreadyRedacted`

For the planned SHIFT implementation, the privacy boundary affects:

- Checkpoint ingestion
- Evidence normalization
- Historical intent extraction
- Invariant authority classification
- Assumption invalidation
- Provider invocation
- Contract rendering
- `why` provenance output
- Verification status reduction
- Redacted/missing-data tests

Entire Graph itself reports that its relevant analysis is local and does not require remote code, hosted models, remote embeddings, or telemetry upload. It can therefore remain part of the local structural-evidence path.

Implementation has not started.

- Loaded transcript and prompt content could be treated as ordinary reasoning input.
- No separate field-level completeness or redaction model was necessary.
- Graph failures could be represented as `UNVERIFIED`.
- Explicit checkpoint input was sufficient for the P0 workflow.
- Commands should remain non-interactive and agent-consumable.
- Graph evidence must be verified against source and tests.

6. Known technical risks

- The original checkpoint had no generated summary; its structured intent was not useful, so reconstruction depended on transcript content.
- `ReadCheckpoint` distinguishes found from missing but does not establish that the returned historical context is complete.
- `SessionContent` exposes `Metadata`, `Transcript`, `TranscriptBlobHashes`, and `Prompts` without an explicit completeness classification.
- Entire’s configured summary path can pass a scoped transcript to a selected generator through `generateCheckpointSummary`.
- Graph ranking was known to be imperfect and required focused source verification.
- Graph reported one unrelated minified JSON parse failure, although its Go impact queries were complete.
- `mise`, `go`, and `gofmt` were unavailable in the checkpoint session, so no build or test had run.
- Seven Codex hooks were still awaiting approval.
- Windows-specific Entire/Graph setup changes remain uncommitted.

## Curveball analysis

### Exact invalidated assumption

The Curveball invalidates this original architectural assumption:

> A successfully retrieved checkpoint with provenance is sufficiently complete and safe to use as authoritative historical context.

That assumption combined two ideas which are no longer valid:

1. Retrieval success implied usable completeness.
2. Raw checkpoint prompts or transcripts could flow into the selected reasoning or summarization provider without a separate privacy boundary.

Under the new requirement, a checkpoint may exist while important fields are redacted or unavailable. A checkpoint ID and provenance reference therefore cannot, by themselves, justify an `EXPLICIT`, complete, or authoritative result.

### Required design change

SHIFT must introduce a first-class context-completeness boundary before historical evidence reaches contract reasoning.

At minimum, evidence needs distinctions such as:

- `COMPLETE`
- `PARTIAL_REDACTED`
- `PARTIAL_MISSING`
- `UNAVAILABLE`

Consequences:

- Redacted or missing evidence may still produce useful, clearly qualified findings.
- Claims derived from partial context cannot become authoritative historical invariants.
- Partial context must force relevant assertions to `INFERRED` or `UNVERIFIED`.
- Verification cannot return `CHANGE VERIFIED` when required historical evidence is incomplete.
- Raw prompts and transcripts must remain local unless an already-approved local processing path satisfies the privacy boundary.
- Any external reasoning path must receive only an explicitly safe, minimized representation—not raw transcript content.

### Graph-identified affected paths

Read-only Graph impact analysis identified these relevant existing paths:

- Checkpoint retrieval:
  - `api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:93` — `ReadCheckpoint`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/aliases.go:66`

- Checkpoint content model:
  - `api/checkpoint/metadata.go:371` — `SessionContent`

- Existing summary/provider path:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1034` — `generateCheckpointSummary`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1111` — `maybeCompactExternalTranscript`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1196` — `generateCheckpointAISummary`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go:83` — provider resolution

- Existing redaction paths:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:442` — redaction configuration
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/redact_cache.go:500` — `RedactTranscriptCached`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/prompts.go:31` — `RedactedJoinedPrompts`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:2507` — redacted checkpoint blob creation
  - `redact/redact.go:112` — `AlreadyRedacted`

For the planned SHIFT implementation, the privacy boundary affects:

- Checkpoint ingestion
- Evidence normalization
- Historical intent extraction
- Invariant authority classification
- Assumption invalidation
- Provider invocation
- Contract rendering
- `why` provenance output
- Verification status reduction
- Redacted/missing-data tests

Entire Graph itself reports that its relevant analysis is local and does not require remote code, hosted models, remote embeddings, or telemetry upload. It can therefore remain part of the local structural-evidence path.

Implementation has not started.

Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

Examples:
  entire graph search --repo . --query "token refresh returns 401" --format text --top-k 8
  entire graph search --repo . --query "csv export ordering" --profile full
Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)

Usage:
  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--relation CALLS] [--direction both|in|out] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 20]

Direct incoming/outgoing relations for one symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at --depth 2. Use it when you want one specific relation/direction; for the full blast radius of a change, prefer impact.

Select a definition with --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME plus --file/--line/--kind when a name is ambiguous. The ambiguity error prints the exact selector for each definition it found.

Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                             Symbol to inspect (required)
  --repo <path>              Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>              Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                 Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>              Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --relation <CALLS>         Relation family to follow (default: CALLS)
  --direction both|in|out    in = callers, out = callees (default: both)
  --depth 1|2                Hops to traverse (default: 1)
  --limit <n>                Max neighbors per direction (default: 20)
  --format json|text|agent   Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>    Output byte budget for agent format (default: 16384)
  --internal-only            Drop unresolved external endpoints
  --exclude-tests            Drop test-only neighbors
  --head                     Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                             Parsing depth (default: full)

Examples:
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --relation CALLS --direction in
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --direction out --depth 2
One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol

Usage:
  entire graph impact --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--depth 1|2] [--limit 15] [--format text|json]

Everything the graph knows about changing one symbol in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth <=2), callees, type consumers (USES_TYPE/PARAM_TYPE/RETURNS_TYPE), data flows, files that historically co-change with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Run this before changing a function/type's behavior.

Ambiguous names return the definition list; rerun with --file/--line/--kind (or --symbol <file>:<line>) to pick one.

Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                            Symbol to analyze (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>             Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>             Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --depth 1|2               Caller-traversal depth (default: 2)
  --limit <n>               Max entries per section (default: 15)
  --format text|json        Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Total text budget (default: 4096)
  --exclude-tests           Drop test-only entries
  --head                    Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth (default: full)

Examples:
  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol WriteText
What a name IS: declaration, fields, and method surface

Usage:
  entire graph def NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--members 15] [--format text|json]

Structural declaration lookup: what a name is and, for a type, its fields and associated-function/method surface, drawn from the graph's own membership edges (inherent impl blocks, receiver methods, extension members, partial parts, one hop of trait/module/base acquisition). It reports a method's owning type, and for a trait/interface it reports who implements it. Membership is never inferred from a name resembling another name.

Arguments:
  NAME|<file>:<line>   Symbol name, or a file:line selector

Flags:
  --repo <path>             Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>             Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>             Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --members <n>             Max members listed per group (default: 15)
  --format text|json        Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Total text budget (default: 4096)
  --head                    Query the committed tree (cached)

Examples:
  entire graph def Result --repo .

Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent

  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)

### Prohibited or guarded path

  → agent CLI or external plugin

  - missing
  - unreadable

  - `PARTIAL_REDACTED`
  - `PARTIAL_MISSING`
  - `UNAVAILABLE`
- Preserve the reason and provenance for every incomplete field.
- Treat checkpoint-read success separately from evidence completeness.
- Permit useful contracts from remaining metadata, summaries, file lists, and local Graph evidence.
- Allow `EXPLICIT` only when the supporting historical evidence is present and inspectable.
- Downgrade unsupported claims to `INFERRED` or `UNVERIFIED`.
- Make completeness explicit and mandatory in both Markdown and JSON.
- Make `VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE` deterministic whenever required historical evidence is partial.
- Keep raw transcript and prompts local.
- Do not use generic summary-provider or external-compactor paths for raw SHIFT evidence.
- If model assistance is retained, pass only a minimized, explicitly safe representation through a provider that satisfies the privacy policy.
- Add tests for:
  - redacted prompt
  - missing transcript
  - missing metadata
  - useful partial contract output
  - refusal to claim authoritative completeness
  - deterministic incomplete verification result
  - identical completeness state in Markdown and JSON

- Existing fully populated checkpoint behavior.
- Graph’s role as structural evidence rather than proof.
- Source and test verification requirements.
- Non-interactive CLI operation.
- Stable invariant identifiers and provenance.
- The three top-level verification outcomes.
- Deterministic authentication demo behavior for complete checkpoints.
- The rule that missing evidence must never be presented as a verified guarantee.

The Graph investigation is complete. The findings are accepted.

Now stop researching and implement the smallest complete change required to incorporate these findings into SHIFT.

Do NOT refactor the existing checkpoint storage system, persistence stores, redaction pipeline, or unrelated Entire CLI behavior.

The preferred architecture is a SHIFT-owned normalization/evidence layer on top of the existing checkpoint APIs.

## Goal

Make SHIFT explicitly understand whether the historical checkpoint evidence it is using is complete, partial, redacted, missing, or unavailable, and prevent SHIFT from presenting unsupported historical claims as verified guarantees.

## Implement

### 1. SHIFT evidence model

Add a SHIFT-owned evidence representation with field-level availability.

Conceptually support:

* AVAILABLE
* REDACTED
* MISSING
* UNREADABLE

For relevant checkpoint evidence such as:

* metadata
* prompts
* transcript

Also derive an aggregate context state such as:

* COMPLETE
* PARTIAL_REDACTED
* PARTIAL_MISSING
* UNAVAILABLE

Use names that fit existing Go conventions if better names already exist.

Do not modify the core checkpoint storage model unless absolutely required.

---

### 2. Evidence normalization

Create an adapter/helper inside SHIFT that consumes the existing checkpoint/session APIs and produces the normalized SHIFT evidence state.

Checkpoint-read success MUST NOT automatically mean evidence completeness.

Preserve reasons for incomplete fields whenever available.

Reuse existing attribution/provenance patterns where helpful, especially the existing handling for missing metadata and fallback context.

---

### 3. Historical-claim rules

SHIFT must enforce:

* `EXPLICIT` only when supporting checkpoint evidence is actually available and inspectable.
* unsupported historical claims must become `INFERRED` or `UNVERIFIED`.
* missing/redacted evidence must never silently become a hard `MUST PRESERVE` guarantee.
* every authoritative invariant must retain provenance.

Keep stable invariant IDs.

---

### 4. Change Contract output

Update SHIFT's Markdown/structured output so evidence completeness is visible.

Example conceptually:

EVIDENCE STATUS

Checkpoint Context: PARTIAL_REDACTED
Metadata: AVAILABLE
Prompt: AVAILABLE
Transcript: REDACTED

INVARIANT INV-02
Status: UNVERIFIED
Reason: supporting transcript unavailable

Do not hide completeness information in verbose debug output.

It should be part of the normal Change Contract.

If JSON output already exists or is part of the current implementation, ensure the same completeness state appears there as well.

Markdown and JSON must not disagree.

---

### 5. Verification behavior

Keep the three existing top-level outcomes:

* CHANGE VERIFIED
* CHANGE BLOCKED
* VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE

Make the result deterministic:

* any required hard invariant FAIL → CHANGE BLOCKED
* no FAIL, but required historical evidence is unavailable/redacted/missing → VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE
* all required evidence and conditions PASS → CHANGE VERIFIED

SHIFT must never return CHANGE VERIFIED when a required historical guarantee depends on unavailable evidence.

---

### 6. Privacy boundary

Do NOT pass raw checkpoint prompts or transcripts through the generic summary-provider path or external transcript-compactor path as part of this change.

Keep raw checkpoint evidence local.

Do not add a new external service.

If the current SHIFT reasoning implementation already invokes an external model with raw historical content, modify that boundary so only a minimized explicitly safe representation is passed, or keep that reasoning local/deterministic for the MVP.

Do not alter Entire's existing summarization behavior globally.

This privacy restriction applies to SHIFT.

---

### 7. Tests

Add focused tests for at least:

1. fully populated checkpoint → COMPLETE
2. missing transcript → PARTIAL_MISSING
3. redacted/unavailable historical evidence → qualified output
4. missing metadata
5. useful Change Contract still generated from remaining evidence
6. unsupported invariant cannot become authoritative EXPLICIT evidence
7. required missing evidence → VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE
8. hard invariant failure → CHANGE BLOCKED
9. complete passing evidence → CHANGE VERIFIED
10. Markdown and JSON represent the same completeness state, if JSON output exists

Prefer table-driven tests where appropriate.

---

## Constraints

Do not:

* rewrite checkpoint persistence
* change existing redaction semantics
* change existing `checkpoint explain` behavior
* change existing attribution behavior
* introduce a new database
* introduce a web service
* create a custom checkpoint storage format
* create a custom graph engine
* send raw transcripts to new external services
* add unrelated features
* perform broad refactors

Graph remains structural evidence, not proof.

Source/tests remain part of verification.

---

## After implementation

Run:

* gofmt on changed Go files
* relevant unit tests
* package tests for SHIFT
* broader tests only where practical
* `go test`/build required to ensure the Entire CLI still compiles

Then report:

1. files changed
2. architecture implemented
3. existing Entire components reused
4. tests added
5. test/build results
6. any limitations
7. whether `entire shift analyze` and `entire shift verify` are now ready for the deterministic demo

Do not continue into unrelated polish or additional features after this task.

Add a SHIFT-owned evidence representation with field-level availability.

Conceptually support:

* AVAILABLE
* REDACTED
* MISSING
* UNREADABLE

For relevant checkpoint evidence such as:

* metadata
* prompts
* transcript

Also derive an aggregate context state such as:

* COMPLETE
* PARTIAL_REDACTED
* PARTIAL_MISSING
* UNAVAILABLE

Use names that fit existing Go conventions if better names already exist.

Do not modify the core checkpoint storage model unless absolutely required.

---

### 2. Evidence normalization

Create an adapter/helper inside SHIFT that consumes the existing checkpoint/session APIs and produces the normalized SHIFT evidence state.

Checkpoint-read success MUST NOT automatically mean evidence completeness.

Preserve reasons for incomplete fields whenever available.

Reuse existing attribution/provenance patterns where helpful, especially the existing handling for missing metadata and fallback context.

---

### 3. Historical-claim rules

SHIFT must enforce:

* `EXPLICIT` only when supporting checkpoint evidence is actually available and inspectable.
* unsupported historical claims must become `INFERRED` or `UNVERIFIED`.
* missing/redacted evidence must never silently become a hard `MUST PRESERVE` guarantee.
* every authoritative invariant must retain provenance.

Keep stable invariant IDs.

---

### 4. Change Contract output

Update SHIFT's Markdown/structured output so evidence completeness is visible.

Example conceptually:

EVIDENCE STATUS

Checkpoint Context: PARTIAL_REDACTED
Metadata: AVAILABLE
Prompt: AVAILABLE
Transcript: REDACTED

INVARIANT INV-02
Status: UNVERIFIED
Reason: supporting transcript unavailable

Do not hide completeness information in verbose debug output.

It should be part of the normal Change Contract.

If JSON output already exists or is part of the current implementation, ensure the same completeness state appears there as well.

Markdown and JSON must not disagree.

---

### 5. Verification behavior

Keep the three existing top-level outcomes:

* CHANGE VERIFIED
* CHANGE BLOCKED
* VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE

Make the result deterministic:

* any required hard invariant FAIL → CHANGE BLOCKED
* no FAIL, but required historical evidence is unavailable/redacted/missing → VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE
* all required evidence and conditions PASS → CHANGE VERIFIED

SHIFT must never return CHANGE VERIFIED when a required historical guarantee depends on unavailable evidence.

---

### 6. Privacy boundary

Do NOT pass raw checkpoint prompts or transcripts through the generic summary-provider path or external transcript-compactor path as part of this change.

Keep raw checkpoint evidence local.

Do not add a new external service.

If the current SHIFT reasoning implementation already invokes an external model with raw historical content, modify that boundary so only a minimized explicitly safe representation is passed, or keep that reasoning local/deterministic for the MVP.

Do not alter Entire's existing summarization behavior globally.

This privacy restriction applies to SHIFT.

---

### 7. Tests

Add focused tests for at least:

1. fully populated checkpoint → COMPLETE
2. missing transcript → PARTIAL_MISSING
3. redacted/unavailable historical evidence → qualified output
4. missing metadata
5. useful Change Contract still generated from remaining evidence
6. unsupported invariant cannot become authoritative EXPLICIT evidence
7. required missing evidence → VERIFICATION INCOMPLETE
8. hard invariant failure → CHANGE BLOCKED
9. complete passing evidence → CHANGE VERIFIED
10. Markdown and JSON represent the same completeness state, if JSON output exists

Prefer table-driven tests where appropriate.

---

## Constraints

Do not:

* rewrite checkpoint persistence
* change existing redaction semantics
* change existing `checkpoint explain` behavior
* change existing attribution behavior
* introduce a new database
* introduce a web service
* create a custom checkpoint storage format
* create a custom graph engine
* send raw transcripts to new external services
* add unrelated features
* perform broad refactors

Graph remains structural evidence, not proof.

Source/tests remain part of verification.

---

## After implementation

Run:

* gofmt on changed Go files
* relevant unit tests
* package tests for SHIFT
* broader tests only where practical
* `go test`/build required to ensure the Entire CLI still compiles

Then report:

1. files changed
2. architecture implemented
3. existing Entire components reused
4. tests added
5. test/build results
6. any limitations
7. whether `entire shift analyze` and `entire shift verify` are now ready for the deterministic demo

Do not continue into unrelated polish or additional features after this task.

  412: 	Model string `json:"model"`

  417: 	TurnID string `json:"turn_id,omitempty"`

  430: 	// CompactTranscriptStart is the line offset in the compact transcript.jsonl
  431: 	// at which this checkpoint's data begins. transcript.jsonl stores the full
  432: 	// compacted session (each checkpoint is self-contained), so readers segment
  433: 	// this checkpoint's slice as compactLines[CompactTranscriptStart:]. The slice
  434: 	// never drops this checkpoint's content, but its first line may repeat up to
  435: 	// one compact line that began in the previous checkpoint (when a streaming
  436: 	// message straddles the boundary and compaction merges it into one line), so
  437: 	// segmenters must tolerate a bounded head overlap.

  440: 	// this checkpoint's delta (CLI versions before the full-compact-transcript
  441: 	// change), which is read as-is from line 0. A pointer is used so that "absent"
  442: 	// (legacy delta file) is distinguishable from 0 (full file, first checkpoint).
  443: 	CompactTranscriptStart *int `json:"compact_transcript_start,omitempty"`

  602:

  606: 	Code     []CodeLearning `json:"code"`     // File/module specific findings

  608: }
  609: 
  610: // CodeLearning captures a learning tied to a specific code location.
  611: type CodeLearning struct {
  612: 	Path    string `json:"path"`               // File path
  613: 	Line    int    `json:"line,omitempty"`     // Start line number
  614: 	EndLine int    `json:"end_line,omitempty"` // End line for ranges (optional)
  615: 	Finding string `json:"finding"`            // What was learned
  616: }
  617: 
  618: // Attribution captures line-level attribution metrics at commit time.

  625: //   - AgentPercentage represents "of the lines changed in this commit, what percentage came from the agent"
  626: //   - AgentRemoved tracks committed deletions performed by the agent
  627: type Attribution struct {

  629: 	AgentLines        int       `json:"agent_lines"`              // Lines added by agent that remain in the commit
  630: 	AgentRemoved      int       `json:"agent_removed"`            // Lines removed by agent that remain removed in the commit

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"context"
